answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the ridge check immediately, the onyx audit keeps the resolved set and the crystal replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 89 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 89 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 33 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
